text:
cust_anna: hey, we've been seeing intermittent signing failures since ~03:00 UTC. errors from our side look like HSM handshake failures and some requests return 502 from the gateway. customer impacted in prod - several transactions retried and some duplicate failures. trace ids: tx-8f3a, tx-8f3b.

alex: sorry to hear that — can you paste the exact error payloads and whether this is Hosted or Private? any recent key imports/rotations? :thinking_face:

cust_anna: hosted API (redwood-hosted), no key rotations on our side. sample error from the client: 
```json
{"error":"signing_error","code":"HSM_HANDSHAKE_FAIL","detail":"tls handshake: EOF"}
```
we also noticed gaps in audit logs around the same time (missing sign events).

alex: thanks. are you seeing this across multiple regions/keys or scoped to a single key/customer region? also pinging @maria for HSM custody/audit implications.

cust_anna: only for key kms://r/prod/az3/key-44; region us-west-2. other keys in the same account are fine.

maria: adding context — if handshake failures are happening under load it could be session exhaustion on the CloudHSM cluster or a transient cert renegotiation issue. missing audit entries are concerning, might be related (if HSM dropped connection before write). can you share timing windows and any request rate changes?

cust_anna: rate jumped from ~150 req/s to ~800 req/s during a batch job at 03:10-03:18 UTC. failures started immediately when spike began.

sam: @alex @maria i'll start a temporary probe of connection counts and queue depth on the gateway. can you ask the customer to run a quick repro check: 
1) capture tcpdump for the timing window (SYN, FIN, RST patterns)
2) run `openssl s_client -connect hsm-proxy.us-west-2.redwood.internal:8443 -status -brief` to see TLS handshake path
3) provide the API request ids (~tx-8f3a etc).

alex: cust_anna — can you share the tcpdump and the gateway logs for 03:05-03:20 UTC and the client stacktrace? if you prefer sftp we can provide a bucket.

cust_anna: uploading pcap now to the support bucket at s3://rw-support-temp/1795554321/pcap.tar.gz. gateway logs attached (snippet):
```
2026-03-15T03:11:59Z gateway sign request id=tx-8f3a state=init
2026-03-15T03:12:00Z gateway hsm_conn id=conn-421 event=handshake_start
2026-03-15T03:12:00Z hsm_conn id=conn-421 event=handshake_fail err=ECONNRESET detail="tls: handshake failure"
2026-03-15T03:12:00Z gateway sign request id=tx-8f3a state=failed err=HSM_HANDSHAKE_FAIL
```

maria: that log pattern + rate spike points to either (a) CloudHSM cluster hitting session/thread limits, or (b) internal load balancer causing connection churn. I'll open an internal CloudHSM runbook check. also important: if audit writes didn't complete we need to know retention implications and whether any keys are in transient 'unlogged' state.

sam: creating an incident for tracking. oncall-bot: INC-2026-314 created, assigned eng-sre + eng-security. attaching initial logs.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-314 — HSM handshake failures under load for customer cust_anna (high). Link: https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-2026-314

alex: next steps for cust_anna: 1) please confirm if you can throttle that batch to <200 req/s while we investigate; 2) share permission to access the full gateway logs and the pcap; 3) if you have recent KMS policy changes share them. we'll aim to have an initial postmortem and mitigation in the incident in 2 hours.

cust_anna: can throttle now, will grant log access. worried about key custody — if the HSM dropped connections mid-sign, is there a chance signatures were partially emitted or keys exposed?

maria: no evidence partial signatures leak key material; HSMs never export private key material. partial operations either succeed or rollback; the bigger risk is missing audit entries. we'll confirm write-ahead logs on CloudHSM and whether redo is possible. we'll also check if any key handle allocations failed.

sam: flagged to infra to scale ephemeral session capacity on the cluster and to confirm LB keepalive settings. i'll update the incident and ping when we have an immediate mitigation. :thumbsup:
